title: HIVE Doctor — Deterministic Symptom→Cause Reasoning Map
author: Jeff
safety: Reference/triage only. Not a diagnosis, prescription, or therapy. Deterministic scoring; medication details reference-only — follow the label and your prescriber. Emergencies: call your local number (911/112/999). Pending clinician sign-off.

urgency_levels.urgent: Be seen today / go to urgent care or ER.
urgency_levels.selfcare: Usually manageable at home with self-care; seek care if it worsens.

fever.label: fever
fever.ask: Do you have a fever or feel hot? Roughly how high if you measured it?
causes: a viral or bacterial infection — a cold, flu, COVID, a tummy bug or a UTI
your body fighting off an infection
watch: a stiff neck, severe headache, or a rash that doesn't fade under a glass
trouble breathing, chest pain, or confusion
any fever in a baby under 3 months, or a child who is floppy, won't drink, or whose fever won't come down
a fever lasting more than 3 days, or very high (over 39.4C / 103F)
care: rest and drink plenty of fluids
paracetamol or ibuprofen can bring the temperature and aches down — follow the label
dress lightly and don't overwrap
look for other symptoms that point to the source

fatigue.label: tiredness / fatigue

it is severe, getting worse, or has lasted many weeks
care: aim for regular sleep and a proper wind-down
eat balanced meals and keep hydrated
gentle regular activity and daylight help
if it lasts weeks, a doctor can check iron, thyroid and more

care: take small, frequent sips of water or an oral rehydration drink
rest your stomach for an hour, then slowly reintroduce bland food
avoid solid food, alcohol, caffeine and fatty food until it settles

care: drink plenty of fluids or an oral rehydration solution

wash hands well to avoid spreading it
most cases settle within a few days without medicine

redflags.msg: These can be signs of a STROKE. Call emergency services (911/112/999) NOW. Note the time symptoms started. Do not give food, drink, or medicine.

Chest pain with these features can be a HEART ATTACK. Call emergency services now. Sit down and rest; if an adult is not allergic and it is available, emergency dispatchers often advise chewing aspirin — follow their instruction.
Swelling of the lips, tongue, or throat can be a life-threatening allergic reaction (ANAPHYLAXIS). Use an adrenaline auto-injector (EpiPen) if available and call emergency services now.
Trouble breathing after an allergen exposure can be ANAPHYLAXIS. Use adrenaline (EpiPen) if available and call emergency services now.
Fever with a stiff neck (especially with headache, light sensitivity, or a rash that doesn't fade under pressure) can be MENINGITIS. Seek emergency care now.
A rash that does NOT fade when pressed (glass test) can signal meningococcal infection. This is an emergency — get help now.
A sudden 'worst-ever' headache that peaks within seconds can be bleeding around the brain. Call emergency services now.
Fever with confusion or very fast breathing can signal serious infection (sepsis). Seek emergency care now.

You matter, and you deserve support right now. If you might act on thoughts of harming yourself, call or text your local crisis line (in the US and Canada, 988) or emergency services. You do not have to face this alone.
CHOKING is an emergency. If the person cannot cough, speak, or breathe, give back blows and abdominal thrusts and call for help now.
Hives together with trouble breathing can be a severe allergic reaction. Use adrenaline (EpiPen) if available and call emergency services now.

Vomiting blood, or black/tarry/sticky stools, can mean bleeding inside the gut (often higher up). Seek urgent medical care — call your local emergency number if you also feel faint, dizzy, or your heart is racing.
New numbness around the groin or loss of bladder/bowel control with back pain is a spinal emergency (cauda equina). Seek emergency care now.
Sudden severe testicle pain can be a torsion that cuts off blood supply — it is time-critical. Seek emergency care now.
Belly pain with vomiting and no gas or stool passing can mean a bowel obstruction. Seek urgent care.
Fruity breath with deep fast breathing in someone with diabetes can be diabetic ketoacidosis. Seek emergency care now.
A severe headache with vision changes and swelling in pregnancy can be pre-eclampsia. Seek emergency care now.
Heavy bleeding after birth is an emergency. Call emergency services now and massage the lower belly firmly.
Uncontrolled heavy bleeding is an emergency. Press hard on the wound with a clean cloth without letting up and call for help now.
Hot dry skin with collapse or confusion can be heat stroke. Cool the person aggressively and call emergency services now.
Severe cold with drowsiness or shivering that has stopped can be hypothermia. Warm gently and seek emergency care.
Sudden breathlessness — especially with a swollen calf, sharp chest pain, or coughing blood — can be a blood clot in the lung (pulmonary embolism). Seek emergency care now.
A suddenly cold, pale, painful, or numb limb can mean a blocked artery — time-critical. Seek emergency care now.
Sudden 'tearing' or 'ripping' chest or back pain can be a tear in the body's main artery (aortic dissection) — call emergency services now.
A painful red eye with vision change or halos can threaten sight (acute glaucoma). Seek same-day emergency eye care.
One-sided pelvic pain in early pregnancy (with or without bleeding) can be an ectopic pregnancy — seek emergency care now.
A severe sore throat with noisy breathing in, drooling, or difficulty swallowing saliva can be a swelling that blocks the airway. Keep calm and upright and call emergency services now.
Pinpoint pupils with slow or absent breathing suggest an opioid overdose. Call emergency services now, give naloxone if available, and start rescue breaths if they aren't breathing.
Someone unresponsive and barely breathing is a life-threatening emergency. Call emergency services now and be ready to start CPR.
Headache, dizziness, and nausea affecting several people or pets in one building — or near fuel-burning appliances — can be carbon monoxide. Get everyone to fresh air and call emergency services now.

Taking too much medicine or a poison needs immediate help. Call emergency services or Poison Control now and keep the container. In the US and Canada call Poison Control 1-800-222-1222; elsewhere call your local poison centre or emergency number.
Snake bite: keep still and calm, keep the limb below heart level, remove tight items, and get to emergency care fast. Don't cut, suck, or use a tourniquet.
A curtain or shadow over part of your vision, or a sudden shower of floaters/flashes, can be a detaching retina — seek same-day emergency eye care to save sight.
Weakness spreading upward from the feet over hours-to-days can affect breathing (Guillain-Barré). Seek emergency care now.
A single hot, swollen, very painful joint with fever can be an infected joint — seek emergency care now; it can damage the joint quickly.
In adrenal insufficiency, vomiting with weakness or confusion can be an adrenal crisis. Use emergency hydrocortisone if prescribed and call emergency services now.
A baby drawing the legs up with episodes of screaming and red 'currant-jelly' stool can be a bowel telescoping (intussusception) — seek emergency care now.
A child with high fever for 5+ days plus red eyes, rash, red cracked lips or a strawberry tongue needs urgent assessment (possible Kawasaki disease).

Bleeding that won't stop or is spurting is an emergency. Press firmly and without stopping directly on the spot with a clean cloth, keep the pressure on, raise the area if you can, and call your local emergency number now.

A deep burn — skin that looks white, brown, charred or leathery, or that has gone numb — is a medical emergency. Call your local emergency number, keep cooling it with cool running water, and cover it loosely with cling film or a clean sheet.
Coughing up a large amount of blood is a medical emergency — call your local emergency number now, sit upright, and if you know which lung it's from, lie on that side.
Coughing up blood always needs to be checked — be seen today (urgent care or ER). Note how much, how often, and any chest pain, breathlessness, fever or weight loss to tell the clinician.

A crushing or heavy pressure in the chest — like a weight or someone sitting on it — can be a HEART ATTACK, especially with sweating, breathlessness, nausea, or pain spreading to the arm, jaw or back. Call your local emergency number now; sit and rest.
Severe difficulty breathing — not being able to get enough air, speak in full sentences, or catch your breath — is an emergency. Call your local emergency number now and sit upright.
Blue lips, face or fingers mean the body isn't getting enough oxygen. Call your local emergency number now.

Fruity or sweet-smelling breath with heavy thirst, lots of urinating, drowsiness or vomiting can be diabetic ketoacidosis — a life-threatening emergency that can happen even if diabetes hasn't been diagnosed yet. Seek emergency care now.
A bad headache with vision changes (blurring, spots) or sudden swelling of the hands/face in pregnancy can be pre-eclampsia — a dangerous rise in blood pressure. Seek emergency care now.

A baby who won't feed, is very sleepy or floppy, or is hard to wake needs to be seen urgently — trust your instinct and get medical help now (emergency care if they are floppy, very pale/blue, or very hard to rouse).

A head injury with vomiting, drowsiness or confusion, a fit, or in someone on blood thinners can mean bleeding inside the skull. Call your local emergency number now and do not leave the person alone.
A swallowed button battery, magnet(s) or sharp object can cause serious internal injury within hours — go to emergency care now. Do not give food or drink or try to make them sick unless told to.
A bulging soft spot, a high-pitched or unusual cry, or a sunken soft spot in a baby can signal serious illness — seek emergency care now.

Few or no wet nappies, no tears, sunken eyes or a sunken soft spot mean a baby may be dehydrated — this needs urgent assessment, especially with vomiting or diarrhoea. Offer small frequent sips and seek care now.

If your baby is moving less or has stopped moving in pregnancy, contact your maternity unit right away (day or night) — do not wait. (If this is about a baby already born who is not moving or responding, call your local emergency number now.)

Severe pain high in the belly or under the right ribs in pregnancy — especially with a headache or feeling very unwell — can be severe pre-eclampsia or HELLP, a dangerous blood-pressure problem. Seek emergency care now.

Numbness between the legs or around the back passage, or losing the feeling of needing to pass urine — especially with back pain or leg weakness — can be cauda equina, a spinal-cord emergency where delay causes permanent damage. Go to emergency care now.
Sudden pain in a testicle — often with belly pain or vomiting — can be a twisted testicle (torsion), which can be saved only if treated within a few hours. Go to emergency care now.

Pain far worse than the wound or skin looks, with spreading redness and feeling very unwell, can be a fast, deep skin infection (necrotising fasciitis). This is an emergency — go now; it spreads in hours.

Pressure, tightness or heaviness in the chest — especially brought on by effort, or with sweating or pain spreading to the arm, jaw or back — can be a HEART ATTACK or angina. Call your local emergency number now; sit and rest.

If an adrenaline auto-injector (EpiPen) was needed, or an allergic reaction is getting worse, call your local emergency number now — go to hospital even if they improve, because the reaction can come back. A second auto-injector can be given after 5 minutes if there's no improvement.

Swallowing bleach, cleaners, antifreeze or similar is an emergency. Do NOT make them vomit or give water unless told to. Call your local emergency number and Poison Control now with the product name. In the US and Canada call Poison Control 1-800-222-1222; elsewhere call your local poison centre or emergency number.

A swallowed poison needs immediate advice. Call your local emergency number and Poison Control now with the product name or a photo; keep the container. Do not make them vomit unless told to. In the US and Canada call Poison Control 1-800-222-1222; elsewhere call your local poison centre or emergency number.
Someone who can't be woken after heavy drinking may have alcohol poisoning. Call your local emergency number now, keep them on their side, and don't leave them alone.

For a chemical burn, rinse with running water for at least 20 minutes and remove contaminated clothing. For a chemical in the eye, keep rinsing and get emergency eye care now. Call your local emergency number or Poison Control.

After an electric shock, make sure the power is off before touching the person. A significant shock needs emergency assessment of the heart and for hidden burns, even if they seem well. Call your local emergency number.
Anyone who nearly drowned should be seen, even if they seem fine — breathing problems can develop over hours. Call your local emergency number if there is any cough, breathlessness or drowsiness.

A low oxygen reading needs prompt assessment — seek urgent care, and call your local emergency number if you are very breathless, your lips look blue, or you feel confused. (Recheck if the hand was cold or the probe loose.)

A fever during chemotherapy, or with a weakened immune system (cancer, transplant, immunosuppressant medicines), can be a life-threatening infection (neutropenic sepsis). Do NOT wait — go to hospital now; you need antibiotics urgently (ideally within an hour). Call your oncology/treatment team's emergency line or your local emergency number.
Very high blood pressure with a sudden severe headache, vision change, chest pain, breathlessness, weakness or a fit can be a hypertensive emergency. Call your local emergency number now.
A painful erection lasting more than a few hours (priapism) is an emergency — go to emergency care now, as delay can cause lasting damage.
A foreskin trapped behind the head of the penis and swelling can cut off blood supply — go to emergency care now.
Spreading redness or infection around a newborn's cord/belly button is an emergency — babies get sick fast. Seek emergency care now.
Skin or a digit turning black or looking dead needs emergency care — the tissue may have lost its blood supply or be badly infected, especially with diabetes or poor circulation.
A fever after travel to a malaria area with confusion, drowsiness, or breathlessness can be severe malaria — an emergency. Go to emergency care now and say where you travelled.
A baby breathing hard who is going blue, not feeding, or pausing in breathing needs emergency care now.

Being unable to pass any urine with a full, painful bladder (acute urinary retention) needs same-day assessment — the bladder needs draining. Go to urgent care; it is an emergency if you also have back pain with numbness between the legs or cannot control your bowels.
A swollen, painful calf together with breathlessness or sharp pain on breathing can mean a clot has travelled to the lungs (pulmonary embolism) — call your local emergency number now.
Black tarry stools with feeling faint, dizzy or very pale can mean significant internal bleeding — call your local emergency number now.
A bulging, tense soft spot on a baby's head can mean dangerously raised pressure in the skull or a serious infection — call your local emergency number or go to the emergency department now.
A lump or abscess near the anus together with fever can mean a spreading infection — be seen today.
A swollen, painful belly with vomiting and no bowel movement or wind can mean a blocked bowel — this needs urgent hospital assessment today. Do not eat or drink until you have been seen.

Drooling, a muffled voice, trouble swallowing saliva, or sitting/leaning forward to breathe can mean a dangerous airway swelling (such as epiglottitis). This is an emergency — call emergency services now and keep the person upright and calm; do not look in the throat.
A sudden, severe, rigid board-like belly that is agony to move or touch can mean a perforation or peritonitis — a surgical emergency. Do not eat or drink and get emergency help now.

Severe, worsening, bursting pain after a fracture or crush — especially with numbness, a tight or swollen limb — can mean compartment syndrome, which can destroy muscle and threaten the limb within hours. Get emergency assessment now; do not elevate the limb above heart level or wait to see if it eases.

A rapidly spreading rash with blistering and skin peeling off in sheets, or raw sore lips and eyes — especially after starting a new medicine — can be a life-threatening skin reaction (such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis). Stop the suspected medicine if advised and get emergency care now.

Cola or tea-coloured urine — especially after intense exercise, a crush injury, or a long time collapsed — can mean muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis) that can harm the kidneys. Get urgent assessment and blood tests, and drink fluids.

Sharp chest pain that is worse breathing in, together with recent immobility (a long flight or journey, or bed rest) or a swollen/painful calf, can mean a clot on the lung (pulmonary embolism). This needs urgent same-day assessment.

A bone through the skin (an open fracture) is an emergency — call your local emergency number now. Do not push the bone back; cover the wound with a clean dressing, control bleeding with pressure around (not on) the bone, keep the limb still, and do not eat or drink in case surgery is needed.

If someone is unresponsive and not breathing normally, this is a cardiac arrest. Call your local emergency number now (put it on speaker) and START CPR: push hard and fast in the centre of the chest, about twice a second, 30 compressions then 2 rescue breaths if you are trained — keep going without stopping until help arrives. Send someone for an AED (defibrillator) if one is nearby and follow its spoken instructions.

During a seizure: protect them from injury, cushion the head, and loosen anything tight around the neck. Do NOT restrain them or put anything in their mouth. Time how long it lasts. When the jerking stops, roll them onto their side (recovery position). Call emergency services now if the seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, one follows another, it is their first seizure, they are injured, pregnant, diabetic, or do not wake up afterwards.

Cool the burn straight away under cool (not ice-cold) running water for at least 20 minutes. Remove jewellery or clothing near the burn unless it is stuck to the skin. Do NOT use ice, butter or creams. Cover loosely with cling film or a clean non-fluffy cloth. Get emergency help for a burn that is large, deep, on the face, hands, feet or genitals, goes all the way round a limb, or came from chemicals, electricity or an airway/inhalation.

A chemical in the eye is an emergency. Rinse the eye immediately with clean, lukewarm running water for at least 15-20 minutes, holding the eyelid open and letting the water run away from the other eye. Remove contact lenses if you can. Do not rub the eye. Keep rinsing on the way to emergency care, and bring the chemical container or its name.

Do NOT pull the object out — it may be plugging the wound and stopping worse bleeding. Call emergency services now. Press firmly AROUND (not on) the object to control bleeding, build up padding either side and bandage around it to hold it still, and keep the person as still as possible.
A sudden 'worst-ever' headache that peaks within seconds can be bleeding around the brain. Call emergency services now.

conditions.name: Possible heart attack / angina (acute coronary syndrome)
conditions.action: Treat chest pressure that spreads to the arm, jaw, or back — with sweating or breathlessness — as a heart attack until proven otherwise. Call emergency services, rest, and follow dispatcher advice.
conditions.red: worsening pain, fainting, breathlessness

conditions.name: Stable angina (exertional chest tightness)
conditions.action: Chest tightness that comes on with exertion and eases with rest suggests angina. Any chest pain at rest, or lasting >10 min, should be treated as an emergency.
conditions.red: pain at rest or lasting >10 minutes

conditions.name: Heart failure (fluid overload)
conditions.action: Breathlessness lying flat, needing extra pillows, with swollen legs suggests fluid overload. See a clinician promptly; sudden severe breathlessness is an emergency.
conditions.red: rapid weight gain, breathless at rest

conditions.name: Atrial fibrillation (irregular fast heartbeat)
conditions.action: An irregular, often fast heartbeat with palpitations may be atrial fibrillation, which raises stroke risk. Get an ECG promptly; fainting or chest pain with it is an emergency.
conditions.red: chest pain, fainting

conditions.name: Deep vein thrombosis (leg clot)
conditions.action: A painful, swollen, warm calf (usually one leg) can be a clot. Seek urgent assessment; sudden breathlessness or chest pain can mean it has moved to the lung — an emergency.
conditions.red: sudden breathlessness or chest pain

conditions.name: Pneumonia (lung infection)
conditions.action: Fever with a productive cough and breathlessness suggests a chest infection. See a clinician promptly; fast breathing, confusion, or blue lips are an emergency.
conditions.red: fast breathing, confusion, blue lips

conditions.name: Asthma flare
conditions.action: Wheeze and breathlessness suggest an asthma flare. Use a reliever inhaler as prescribed and sit upright. If it doesn't ease, speech is broken, or lips go blue, call emergency services.
conditions.red: no relief from inhaler, can't speak in sentences

conditions.name: COPD flare
conditions.action: In known COPD, increasing breathlessness and sputum suggests a flare. Use prescribed inhalers and seek prompt care; severe breathlessness or confusion is an emergency.
conditions.red: confusion, severe breathlessness

conditions.name: Acute bronchitis
conditions.action: A cough (often with phlegm) after a cold, with no breathlessness, is usually viral bronchitis that settles in 1-3 weeks. Antibiotics rarely help. See care if breathless or fever persists.
conditions.red: breathlessness, high or lasting fever

conditions.name: Common cold / upper respiratory infection
conditions.action: A runny nose, sore throat, and mild cough point to a common cold. Rest, fluids, and OTC symptom relief help; see the medication reference and follow the label. See care if it worsens after a week.
conditions.red: symptoms worsening after 7-10 days

conditions.name: Influenza (flu)
conditions.action: Sudden fever, body aches, and exhaustion suggest flu. Rest and fluids; antivirals help most if started early in high-risk people. Seek care for breathlessness or chest pain.
conditions.red: breathlessness, chest pain, confusion

conditions.name: COVID-19
conditions.action: Fever, cough, and fatigue may be COVID-19 — testing confirms it. Isolate and rest; seek urgent care for breathlessness or low oxygen.
conditions.red: breathlessness, low oxygen, chest pain

conditions.name: Sinusitis
conditions.action: Facial pressure and congestion suggest sinusitis, usually viral. Saline rinses and decongestants help; most clears in ~10 days. See care if severe, one-sided, or with eye swelling.
conditions.red: eye swelling, severe one-sided pain

conditions.name: Strep throat
conditions.action: A very sore throat with fever and no cough can be strep, which may need antibiotics after a test. See a clinician; difficulty breathing or swallowing saliva is an emergency.
conditions.red: can't swallow saliva, trouble breathing

conditions.name: Appendicitis
conditions.action: Pain that began near the navel and settled in the lower right belly, with nausea and low fever, suggests appendicitis. Seek urgent surgical assessment; do not eat in case surgery is needed.
conditions.red: spreading pain, high fever, rigid belly

conditions.name: Gastroenteritis / food poisoning
conditions.action: Vomiting and diarrhea are usually a self-limiting gut infection. The priority is fluids — sip oral rehydration. See care for signs of dehydration, blood in stool, or symptoms beyond a few days.
conditions.red: dehydration, blood in stool, >3 days

conditions.name: Acid reflux (GERD)
conditions.action: Burning behind the breastbone, worse lying down or after meals, suggests reflux. Smaller meals, not lying down after eating, and OTC antacids help. Chest pain with exertion needs emergency review to rule out the heart.
conditions.red: exertional pain, trouble swallowing, weight loss

conditions.name: Gastritis / peptic ulcer
conditions.action: Upper-middle belly burning or gnawing can be gastritis or an ulcer. Avoid NSAIDs and alcohol; see a clinician. Black stools or vomiting blood is an emergency.
conditions.red: black stools, vomiting blood

conditions.name: Gallstones / biliary colic
conditions.action: Right-upper-belly pain after fatty meals suggests gallstones. See a clinician; pain with fever and jaundice is an emergency (infected bile duct).
conditions.red: fever + jaundice with the pain

conditions.name: Kidney stone
conditions.action: Severe one-sided flank pain that comes in waves, often with blood in the urine, suggests a kidney stone. Fluids and pain relief help; fever with it, or inability to keep fluids down, needs urgent care.
conditions.red: fever, can't keep fluids down

conditions.name: Irritable bowel syndrome
conditions.action: Recurrent cramping with bloating and changed bowel habit, relieved by passing stool, suggests IBS. Diet and stress management help. New symptoms over age 50, weight loss, or blood need review first.
conditions.red: blood in stool, weight loss, new onset over 50

conditions.name: Constipation
conditions.action: Infrequent hard stools usually respond to fluids, fibre, and movement. See the medication reference for stool softeners and follow the label. Pain with no gas/stool and vomiting needs urgent care.
conditions.red: vomiting with no gas or stool passing

conditions.name: Hemorrhoids
conditions.action: Bright blood on the paper or stool surface, with itch or a lump, is usually hemorrhoids. Fibre, fluids, and warm baths help. Darker blood mixed in stool, or weight loss, needs review to exclude other causes.
conditions.red: dark blood mixed in stool, weight loss

conditions.name: Migraine
conditions.action: A one-sided throbbing headache with light sensitivity, nausea, or visual aura suggests migraine. Rest in a dark quiet room; see the medication reference for options and follow the label. A sudden 'worst-ever' headache is an emergency.
conditions.red: sudden worst-ever headache, weakness, confusion

conditions.name: Tension headache
conditions.action: A band-like, both-sided, pressing headache without nausea or aura is usually a tension headache. Rest, fluids, and simple pain relief help. New, severe, or changing headaches need review.
conditions.red: new pattern, severe, with fever or weakness

conditions.name: Stroke / TIA
conditions.action: Face drooping, arm weakness, or speech trouble is a stroke until proven otherwise — act FAST. Call emergency services immediately and note the start time.
conditions.red: any face/arm/speech change

conditions.name: Meningitis
conditions.action: Fever with a stiff neck, severe headache, and light sensitivity can be meningitis. Seek emergency care now; a rash that doesn't fade under pressure is especially urgent.
conditions.red: non-fading rash, drowsiness

conditions.name: Concussion
conditions.action: A knock to the head with headache, confusion, or nausea suggests concussion. Rest and watch closely. Repeated vomiting, worsening drowsiness, one big pupil, or a seizure means emergency care now.
conditions.red: repeated vomiting, worsening drowsiness, seizure

conditions.name: Vertigo (BPPV / inner ear)
conditions.action: A spinning sensation triggered by head movement is often an inner-ear cause. It usually settles; repositioning exercises help. Vertigo with face/arm/speech change, deafness, or severe headache needs emergency review.
conditions.red: with weakness, slurred speech, or severe headache

conditions.name: Sciatica
conditions.action: Pain shooting from the back down one leg, sometimes with tingling, suggests a pinched nerve. Keep gently moving; most settles in weeks. Numb groin or loss of bladder/bowel control is a spinal emergency.
conditions.red: numb groin, bladder/bowel control loss

conditions.name: Seizure
conditions.action: During a seizure, protect the head, don't restrain, and time it. Call emergency services for a first seizure, one lasting over 5 minutes, repeated seizures, injury, or if the person doesn't wake up.
conditions.red: lasting >5 min, first-ever, not waking

conditions.name: Urinary tract infection
conditions.action: Burning and frequent urination suggest a bladder infection, which may need antibiotics. Fluids help. Fever, flank/back pain, or vomiting suggests the kidney is involved — seek urgent care.
conditions.red: fever, flank pain, vomiting

conditions.name: Kidney infection
conditions.action: Fever and chills with flank pain and urinary burning suggest a kidney infection, which needs prompt antibiotics. Seek urgent care; confusion or inability to keep fluids down is an emergency.
conditions.red: confusion, can't keep fluids down

conditions.name: Possible fracture (broken bone)
conditions.action: Pain, swelling, and especially visible deformity or inability to use the limb after injury suggests a fracture. Immobilize and support it. Bone through skin, a cold/blue limb, or suspected neck/back injury is an emergency.
conditions.red: open wound over bone, cold/blue limb, spine injury

conditions.name: Sprain / strain
conditions.action: A twist with swelling and bruising but no deformity is usually a sprain. Rest, ice, compression, elevation. If you can't bear weight at all or there's marked deformity, get it X-rayed to exclude a fracture.
conditions.red: can't bear weight at all, deformity

conditions.name: Mechanical low back pain
conditions.action: Back pain after lifting or twisting, without leg weakness or bladder changes, is usually muscular and improves with gentle movement and time. Red flags (leg weakness, numb groin, fever, trauma) need review.
conditions.red: leg weakness, numb groin, fever, major trauma

conditions.name: Gout
conditions.action: A sudden, very painful, hot, swollen joint (often the big toe) suggests gout. Rest and anti-inflammatories help if appropriate. A hot swollen joint with fever could be a joint infection — seek urgent care to be sure.
conditions.red: fever with the hot joint (possible infection)

conditions.name: Osteoarthritis
conditions.action: Gradual joint pain and stiffness that worsens with use and improves with rest suggests osteoarthritis. Movement, weight management, and pain relief help. A hot, suddenly swollen joint is a different, urgent problem.
conditions.red: sudden hot swollen joint, fever

conditions.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
conditions.action: Symmetrical small-joint pain and stiffness lasting over an hour each morning may be inflammatory arthritis. Early specialist review protects the joints — see a clinician.
conditions.red: prolonged morning stiffness, many joints

conditions.name: Cellulitis (skin infection)
conditions.action: Spreading red, warm, tender skin — often with fever — suggests cellulitis, which usually needs antibiotics. Mark the edge and see a clinician promptly. Rapid spread, blistering, or severe pain is an emergency.
conditions.red: rapid spread, blistering, severe pain

conditions.name: Shingles
conditions.action: A painful blistering rash in a band on one side of the body suggests shingles. Antiviral medicine works best started within 72 hours — see a clinician promptly. Shingles near the eye needs urgent care.
conditions.red: rash near the eye, widespread blisters

conditions.name: Hives (urticaria)
conditions.action: Itchy raised welts that come and go are usually hives, often from an allergy or infection. Antihistamines help — see the medication reference and follow the label. Swelling of lips/tongue or breathing trouble is an emergency.
conditions.red: lip/tongue swelling, trouble breathing

conditions.name: Eczema
conditions.action: Dry, itchy, inflamed patches in the skin creases suggest eczema. Regular moisturizers and avoiding triggers help; short courses of steroid cream are used for flares. Weeping, crusted, painful skin may be infected.
conditions.red: weeping, crusting, spreading redness

conditions.name: Skin abscess / boil
conditions.action: A painful lump filling with pus is an abscess; many need draining by a clinician. Warm compresses help early. Spreading redness, fever, or facial location needs prompt care.
conditions.red: fever, spreading redness, face

conditions.name: Anaphylaxis (severe allergic reaction)
conditions.action: A severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) is an emergency. Use an adrenaline auto-injector (EpiPen) into the outer thigh straight away if you have one, and call your local emergency number now. Lie the person flat with legs raised (sit up if breathing is hard); if there's no improvement in 5 minutes, give a second auto-injector. Even if they recover, they must be seen — symptoms can come back (biphasic).
conditions.red: any airway swelling or breathing trouble

conditions.name: Burn / scald
conditions.action: Cool the burn straight away under cool (not ice-cold) running water for 20 minutes, and remove any jewellery or clothing near it that isn't stuck to the skin. Don't use ice, butter, toothpaste or creams. Cover it loosely with cling film laid over (not wrapped tight) or a clean non-fluffy dressing, and use simple pain relief. The degrees: a superficial (first-degree) burn is red, dry and painful and usually heals at home; a partial-thickness (second-degree) burn blisters and weeps — don't burst the blisters; a full-thickness (third-degree) burn looks white, brown or charred and leathery and may feel numb, and needs emergency care.
conditions.red: Get urgent care for any burn bigger than the person's hand, or on the face, hands, feet, genitals or over a joint, blistering in a child, or any chemical or electrical burn. Call emergency services for a deep (white/charred/leathery) burn, a burn circling a limb, soot or burns around the nose or mouth, a hoarse voice or trouble breathing, or if the person is very unwell.

conditions.name: Heat stroke
conditions.action: Hot skin with confusion or collapse in heat is a medical emergency. Move to shade, cool aggressively (water, fanning, ice packs to neck/armpits/groin), and call emergency services now.
conditions.red: confusion, collapse, hot skin

conditions.name: Hypothermia
conditions.action: Severe cold with drowsiness, confusion, or shivering that has stopped is dangerous. Move somewhere warm, remove wet clothing, wrap the person, and seek emergency care; handle gently.
conditions.red: drowsiness, shivering stopped

conditions.name: Dehydration
conditions.action: Dry mouth, little/dark urine, and dizziness point to dehydration. Sip oral rehydration steadily. No urine, sunken eyes, drowsiness, or inability to keep fluids down needs urgent care — especially in children.
conditions.red: no urine, drowsiness, can't keep fluids down

conditions.name: Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)
conditions.action: Shakiness, sweating, and confusion — especially in someone on diabetes medicine — suggest low blood sugar. If awake and able to swallow, give fast sugar (juice, glucose) now and recheck. If drowsy or fitting, call emergency services.
conditions.red: drowsy, can't swallow, seizure

conditions.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis / high sugar crisis
conditions.action: High thirst, deep fast breathing, fruity breath, and vomiting in diabetes can be ketoacidosis — an emergency. Seek emergency care now.
conditions.red: deep breathing, drowsiness, vomiting

conditions.name: Possible new diabetes
conditions.action: Excessive thirst, frequent urination, and unexplained weight loss can signal diabetes. See a clinician for a blood sugar test promptly.
conditions.red: vomiting, deep breathing, drowsiness

conditions.name: Underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism)
conditions.action: Feeling cold, sluggish, and tired with weight gain can point to an underactive thyroid. A blood test confirms it — see a clinician.
conditions.red: chest pain, very slow pulse, drowsiness or feeling very cold and confused (rare severe cases)

conditions.name: Overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism)
conditions.action: Feeling hot, racing heart, weight loss despite eating, and anxiety can point to an overactive thyroid. A blood test confirms it — see a clinician.
conditions.red: a racing or irregular heartbeat, fever and agitation, or chest pain

conditions.name: Anemia
conditions.action: Tiredness, breathlessness on exertion, and pallor can mean a low blood count. A blood test finds the cause — see a clinician. Black stools or heavy bleeding with these needs urgent review.
conditions.red: black stools, heavy bleeding

conditions.name: Depression
conditions.action: Persistent low mood and loss of interest most days for two weeks or more may be depression — a treatable medical condition. Talking therapies and/or medication help. You deserve support; please reach out to a clinician.
conditions.red: thoughts of self-harm — seek help now

conditions.name: Anxiety
conditions.action: Constant worry, restlessness, and physical tension that interfere with life may be an anxiety disorder. Breathing techniques, therapy, and sometimes medication help — a clinician can guide you.
conditions.red: chest pain or first-ever episode — rule out physical causes

conditions.name: Panic attack
conditions.action: A sudden surge of fear with pounding heart, breathlessness, and a sense of doom that peaks in minutes is a panic attack — intense but not dangerous. Slow breathing helps. A first-ever episode should be checked to rule out heart or lung causes.
conditions.red: first-ever, or with true chest pain

conditions.name: Post-traumatic stress
conditions.action: Flashbacks, nightmares, and feeling on edge after a traumatic event may be PTSD. Trauma-focused therapy is effective — a clinician can help you find it.
conditions.red: thoughts of self-harm — seek help now

conditions.name: Grief
conditions.action: Grief after a loss brings waves of sadness, and there's no fixed timeline. Support from people you trust helps. If it becomes hopelessness, or you have thoughts of self-harm, please reach out for help.
conditions.red: hopelessness, thoughts of self-harm

conditions.name: Active labor
conditions.action: Regular strengthening contractions or waters breaking signal labor. Contact your maternity unit. If birth is imminent (baby crowning) and you can't reach help, follow the emergency childbirth guide and call emergency services.
conditions.red: crowning, cord or limb first, heavy bleeding

conditions.name: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever)
conditions.action: Sneezing, a runny/itchy nose, and itchy watery eyes — often seasonal or with pets/dust — suggest allergy. Antihistamines and avoiding triggers help; see the medication reference and follow the label.
conditions.red: wheeze or breathlessness (possible asthma)

conditions.name: Tonsillitis
conditions.action: A very sore throat with fever and swollen neck glands suggests tonsillitis, often viral. Fluids and pain relief help; a swab may be needed. Trouble breathing, drooling, or unable to swallow saliva is an emergency.
conditions.red: drooling, can't swallow saliva, trouble breathing

conditions.name: Middle ear infection
conditions.action: Ear pain with fever, often after a cold, suggests a middle-ear infection. Pain relief helps and many clear on their own; see a clinician if severe, not improving in 2–3 days, or with discharge or swelling behind the ear.
conditions.red: swelling/redness behind the ear, stiff neck

conditions.name: Conjunctivitis (pink eye)
conditions.action: A red, gritty, watery or sticky eye is usually conjunctivitis, often viral and self-limiting. Clean the lids gently and avoid sharing towels. Pain, blurred vision, or light sensitivity needs same-day eye assessment.
conditions.red: eye pain, vision loss, light sensitivity

conditions.name: Acute angle-closure glaucoma
conditions.action: A painful red eye with blurred vision, halos around lights, headache, and vomiting can be a sight-threatening pressure rise. Seek emergency eye care now.
conditions.red: any painful red eye with vision loss

conditions.name: Laryngitis
conditions.action: A hoarse or lost voice with a cold is usually viral laryngitis; rest the voice and fluids help. Hoarseness lasting over 3 weeks should be checked.
conditions.red: hoarseness lasting over 3 weeks

conditions.name: Pleurisy
conditions.action: Sharp chest pain that is worse with breathing in suggests inflamed lung lining, often after a viral infection. See a clinician; sudden severe breathlessness, a swollen calf, or coughing blood needs emergency care.
conditions.red: sudden breathlessness, calf swelling, coughing blood

conditions.name: Tuberculosis (consider)
conditions.action: A cough lasting weeks with night sweats, weight loss, and sometimes blood can suggest TB, especially with known exposure or risk. See a clinician promptly for testing; avoid close contact until assessed.
conditions.red: coughing blood, breathlessness

conditions.name: Pericarditis
conditions.action: Sharp chest pain that eases leaning forward and worsens lying down or breathing in suggests inflamed heart lining. See urgent care to assess; any chest pain with collapse, severe breathlessness, or spreading to the arm is an emergency.
conditions.red: breathlessness, fainting, arm/jaw pain

conditions.name: Aortic dissection (consider)
conditions.action: Sudden 'tearing' or 'ripping' severe chest or back pain can be a tear in the body's main artery — immediately life-threatening. Call emergency services now.
conditions.red: any sudden tearing chest/back pain

conditions.name: Very high blood pressure
conditions.action: A very high blood-pressure reading needs assessment, urgently if with chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache, vision change, weakness, or confusion (these suggest organ damage — an emergency).
conditions.red: chest pain, breathlessness, vision/speech change

conditions.name: Peripheral arterial disease
conditions.action: Calf or leg pain that comes on with walking and eases with rest suggests narrowed leg arteries. Stopping smoking, exercise, and risk-factor control help — see a clinician. A suddenly cold, pale, painful leg is an emergency.
conditions.red: sudden cold pale painful leg (acute blockage)

conditions.name: Pancreatitis
conditions.action: Severe upper-belly pain boring through to the back with vomiting suggests pancreatitis, often from gallstones or alcohol. Seek urgent care; do not eat or drink until assessed.
conditions.red: severe pain, fever, can't keep fluids down

conditions.name: Gallbladder infection (cholecystitis)
conditions.action: Right-upper-belly pain with fever (and sometimes jaundice) suggests an infected gallbladder. Seek urgent care; jaundice with fever and pain is an emergency (infected bile duct).
conditions.red: jaundice + fever with the pain

conditions.name: Diverticulitis
conditions.action: Left-lower-belly pain with fever and a change in bowel habit suggests diverticulitis. See urgent care; severe pain, a rigid belly, or heavy rectal bleeding is an emergency.
conditions.red: rigid belly, heavy bleeding, high fever

conditions.name: Hepatitis (liver inflammation)
conditions.action: Yellowing skin/eyes with tiredness, nausea, and right-upper-belly discomfort suggests liver inflammation (viral, alcohol, or drug-related). See a clinician promptly; confusion or bleeding is an emergency.
conditions.red: confusion, bleeding, severe vomiting

conditions.name: Anal fissure
conditions.action: Sharp pain on passing stool with a streak of bright blood on the paper suggests a small tear. Softening stool (fibre, fluids) and warm baths help it heal. Blood mixed in the stool or weight loss needs review. Any new rectal bleeding should be checked by a clinician to confirm the cause and rule out anything more serious, even when a fissure or piles is likely.
conditions.red: blood mixed in stool, weight loss

conditions.name: Lactose intolerance
conditions.action: Bloating, wind, and loose stools after milk or dairy suggest lactose intolerance. Reducing lactose or using lactase helps. Weight loss, blood, or night symptoms need review for other causes.
conditions.red: weight loss, blood in stool

conditions.name: Prostatitis
conditions.action: Pelvic/perineal pain with urinary burning, difficulty, and fever in men suggests prostate inflammation/infection. See a clinician promptly; inability to pass urine at all, or high fever and feeling very unwell, is an emergency.
conditions.red: can't pass urine at all, high fever, rigors

conditions.name: Enlarged prostate (BPH)
conditions.action: A weak stream, straining, dribbling, and night-time urination in older men suggest an enlarged prostate. It's common and treatable — see a clinician. Sudden inability to pass urine is an emergency.
conditions.red: sudden inability to pass urine (retention)

conditions.name: Sexually transmitted infection
conditions.action: New discharge, burning, or bleeding after sex can be an STI. Testing and treatment are confidential and important — see a clinician or sexual-health service, and avoid sex until treated. Partners may need treating too.
conditions.red: fever, severe pelvic pain, pregnant

conditions.name: Pelvic inflammatory disease
conditions.action: Lower-pelvic pain with fever and abnormal discharge can be a pelvic infection that needs prompt antibiotics to protect fertility. Seek urgent care; severe pain with fever and vomiting is an emergency.
conditions.red: severe pain, high fever, pregnant

conditions.name: Ovarian cyst
conditions.action: One-sided pelvic pain can come from an ovarian cyst, often harmless. See a clinician for persistent pain. Sudden severe one-sided pain with vomiting can be a twisted ovary (torsion) — an emergency.
conditions.red: sudden severe one-sided pain + vomiting (torsion)

conditions.name: Ectopic pregnancy (consider)
conditions.action: One-sided pelvic pain with bleeding in early pregnancy (or a positive test) can be an ectopic pregnancy — life-threatening if it ruptures. Seek emergency care now.
conditions.red: shoulder-tip pain, faintness, heavy bleeding

conditions.name: Period pain (dysmenorrhea)
conditions.action: Cramping lower-belly pain with periods is common. Heat, gentle activity, and anti-inflammatories help — see the medication reference and follow the label. Pain that is severe, new, or with heavy bleeding or fever needs review.
conditions.red: severe/new pain, fever, pregnancy

conditions.name: Cluster headache
conditions.action: Severe one-sided pain around the eye with a watering eye or blocked nostril, in bouts, suggests cluster headache. See a clinician for specific treatment; a first severe headache should be assessed to exclude other causes.
conditions.red: first-ever, worst-ever, or with weakness/fever

conditions.name: Giant cell arteritis (consider)
conditions.action: A new headache in someone over ~50 with scalp tenderness and jaw ache on chewing can be giant cell arteritis, which can threaten sight. Seek urgent care the same day; sudden vision loss is an emergency.
conditions.red: any vision loss

conditions.name: Bell's palsy
conditions.action: Sudden one-sided facial weakness that includes the forehead, without arm/leg or speech problems, may be Bell's palsy. Because facial droop can also be a stroke, it must be assessed urgently to be sure — do not wait.
conditions.red: arm/leg weakness or speech change (treat as stroke)

conditions.name: Parkinson's disease
conditions.action: A resting tremor with slowness and stiffness that came on gradually can suggest Parkinson's. See a clinician for assessment — treatments help symptoms.
conditions.red: sudden weakness or speech change (different, urgent)

conditions.name: Memory loss / dementia (assess)
conditions.action: Progressive memory and thinking changes that affect daily life deserve assessment — some causes are treatable. See a clinician. Sudden confusion is different and may be an emergency (infection, stroke).
conditions.red: sudden confusion (urgent — infection/stroke)

conditions.name: Trigeminal neuralgia
conditions.action: Brief electric-shock-like facial pains triggered by touch, chewing, or wind suggest trigeminal neuralgia. Specific medicines help — see a clinician.
conditions.red: weakness, rash, or fever with the pain

conditions.name: Fibromyalgia
conditions.action: Widespread body pain with fatigue, poor sleep, and tenderness suggests fibromyalgia. Paced exercise, sleep, and stress care help — see a clinician. New localized pain, weight loss, or fever needs separate review.
conditions.red: weight loss, fever, focal weakness

conditions.name: Polymyalgia rheumatica
conditions.action: New shoulder and hip stiffness, worst in the morning, in someone over ~50 suggests polymyalgia rheumatica, which responds well to treatment. See a clinician; headache with scalp tenderness or jaw pain needs urgent review (arteritis).
conditions.red: new headache, scalp tenderness, vision change

conditions.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
conditions.action: Numbness and tingling in the thumb-side fingers, worse at night, suggests carpal tunnel. Wrist splints and activity changes help — see a clinician if persistent or with weakness/wasting.
conditions.red: hand weakness or muscle wasting

conditions.name: Plantar fasciitis
conditions.action: Heel pain that's sharpest on the first steps of the day suggests plantar fasciitis. Calf and foot stretches, supportive shoes, and rest help over weeks.
conditions.red: numbness, fever, or pain after acute injury

conditions.name: Impetigo
conditions.action: Golden-crusted sores, often around the nose/mouth and common in children, suggest impetigo, a contagious bacterial skin infection usually needing antibiotic cream or tablets. See a clinician; keep the area clean and avoid sharing towels.
conditions.red: spreading redness, fever, feeling unwell

conditions.name: Scabies
conditions.action: Intense itching that's worse at night, with a rash in finger webs, wrists, and waist, suggests scabies. It's treatable with a prescribed cream/wash — the whole household is usually treated. See a clinician.
conditions.red: widespread crusting, immune problems

conditions.name: Ringworm (tinea)
conditions.action: A ring-shaped, scaly, itchy patch with a clearer centre suggests a fungal infection. Antifungal creams clear it; keep skin dry. Scalp or widespread involvement, or no improvement, needs a clinician.
conditions.red: scalp involvement, spreading, no improvement

conditions.name: Measles (consider)
conditions.action: High fever with cough, runny nose, red eyes, then a spreading blotchy rash can be measles, which is very contagious. Phone ahead before attending so others aren't exposed; seek urgent care for breathing trouble or drowsiness.
conditions.red: breathing trouble, drowsiness, dehydration

conditions.name: Glandular fever (mononucleosis)
conditions.action: A severe sore throat with marked fatigue and swollen glands, often in teens/young adults, suggests glandular fever. Rest and fluids; avoid contact sport while the spleen may be enlarged. Trouble breathing/swallowing or severe belly pain needs urgent care.
conditions.red: trouble breathing/swallowing, severe left-upper belly pain

conditions.name: Lyme disease (consider)
conditions.action: An expanding bullseye rash after a tick bite, sometimes with flu-like symptoms, suggests early Lyme disease, which is treated with antibiotics. See a clinician promptly. Facial droop, severe headache, or palpitations need urgent review.
conditions.red: facial droop, severe headache, palpitations

conditions.name: Bipolar spectrum (assess)
conditions.action: Periods of elevated, racing, high-energy mood with little need for sleep, alternating with low periods, may suggest a bipolar pattern. An assessment helps — treatment stabilizes mood. Reckless risk to safety needs urgent help.
conditions.red: risk to safety, psychosis — seek urgent help

conditions.name: Possible psychosis
conditions.action: Hearing or seeing things others don't, or strong fixed fearful beliefs, can be signs of psychosis — which is treatable. Reach out for urgent mental-health assessment. If there is danger to anyone, call emergency services.
conditions.red: danger to self or others — call emergency services

conditions.name: Disordered eating (reach out)
conditions.action: If eating, weight, or body image feel out of control or distressing, you deserve support — eating difficulties are treatable and you don't have to manage alone. Please reach out to a clinician or a specialist helpline.
conditions.red: fainting, chest palpitations, very low intake — seek care

conditions.name: Insomnia
conditions.action: Ongoing trouble falling or staying asleep responds well to sleep habits (consistent times, wind-down, limiting screens/caffeine) — the first-line approach. Persistent insomnia, or with low mood or snoring/pauses in breathing, should be reviewed.
conditions.red: loud snoring with breathing pauses, low mood

conditions.name: Alcohol withdrawal
conditions.action: Tremor, sweating, anxiety, and nausea after cutting down heavy alcohol can be withdrawal, which can become dangerous (seizures, confusion). Don't stop abruptly alone — seek medical help to withdraw safely; confusion or a seizure is an emergency.
conditions.red: confusion, hallucinations, seizure (emergency)

conditions.name: Heat exhaustion
conditions.action: Heavy sweating, dizziness, nausea, and weakness in heat is heat exhaustion. Move somewhere cool, lie down, raise the legs, sip fluids, and cool the skin. If skin becomes hot and dry, confusion sets in, or there's no improvement in 30 minutes, treat as heat stroke — an emergency.
conditions.red: hot dry skin, confusion, collapse (heat stroke)

conditions.name: Frostbite
conditions.action: White, waxy, hard, numb skin after cold exposure is frostbite. Get warm, remove wet/tight items, and rewarm the area in warm (not hot) water; don't rub. Seek care; blackened skin or whole-body cold (hypothermia) is an emergency.
conditions.red: blackened skin, drowsiness, whole-body cold

conditions.name: Croup
conditions.action: A barking cough with a harsh noise breathing in, usually in young children at night, suggests croup. Keep the child calm and upright; cool/steamy air may ease it. Noisy breathing at rest, drooling, blue lips, or severe struggle to breathe is an emergency.
conditions.red: stridor at rest, drooling, blue lips

conditions.name: Bronchiolitis (infants)
conditions.action: In babies, a cold that leads to fast, wheezy, laboured breathing and feeding difficulty suggests bronchiolitis. Watch breathing and feeding closely. Fast breathing, ribs sucking in, pauses in breathing, blue lips, or poor feeding needs urgent care.
conditions.red: ribs sucking in, breathing pauses, blue lips, poor feeding

conditions.name: Seizure brought on by a fever (febrile seizure, in young children)
conditions.action: A brief seizure during a fever in a young child is frightening but often not dangerous. Protect from injury, lay on the side, time it, and don't restrain. Call emergency services for a first seizure, one over 5 minutes, repeated seizures, or if the child doesn't recover.
conditions.red: >5 minutes, repeated, not recovering, first-ever

conditions.name: Severe pregnancy vomiting
conditions.action: Severe, persistent vomiting in pregnancy can cause dehydration (hyperemesis). Sip fluids; see urgent care if you can't keep fluids down, pass little/dark urine, or feel faint — you may need rehydration.
conditions.red: can't keep fluids down, little/dark urine, faint

conditions.name: Breast change worth checking
conditions.action: A new breast lump or nipple change should be checked — most are not cancer, but they need assessment. See a clinician; see the oncology reference for the warning signs and screening.
conditions.red: skin dimpling, bloody nipple discharge

conditions.name: Bowel change worth checking
conditions.action: A lasting change in bowel habit, blood in the stool, or unexplained weight loss should be checked to rule out serious causes including bowel cancer. See a clinician; most causes are not cancer.
conditions.red: ongoing bleeding, weight loss, anaemia

conditions.name: Persistent cough worth checking
conditions.action: A cough lasting over 3 weeks, coughing blood, or unexplained weight loss should be checked — especially with a smoking history. See a clinician; this rules out serious causes including lung cancer.
conditions.red: coughing blood, breathlessness, weight loss

conditions.name: Changing mole worth checking
conditions.action: A mole that is changing, bleeding, or looks different from your others should be checked (the ABCDE signs). See a clinician — early skin cancers are very treatable.
conditions.red: bleeding, rapid change, irregular borders

conditions.name: A lump or swollen gland worth checking
conditions.action: A new, growing, or persistent lump or swollen gland — especially with night sweats or weight loss — should be assessed. See a clinician; this checks for causes including lymphoma and other cancers.
conditions.red: night sweats, weight loss, persistent nodes

conditions.name: Blood in the urine worth checking
conditions.action: Visible blood in the urine — even once and even if painless — should always be checked. See a clinician; causes range from infection and stones to bladder or kidney cancer.
conditions.red: any visible blood in urine

conditions.name: Abnormal bleeding worth checking
conditions.action: Bleeding after menopause, after sex, or between periods should be checked. See a clinician; most causes are benign, but this rules out cervical and uterine cancers.
conditions.red: any post-menopausal bleeding

conditions.name: Difficulty swallowing worth checking
conditions.action: New or worsening difficulty swallowing should be checked promptly. See a clinician; causes include reflux strictures and, less commonly, oesophageal or stomach cancer.
conditions.red: food sticking, weight loss, vomiting

conditions.name: Painless jaundice worth urgent checking
conditions.action: Yellowing of the skin/eyes without pain, especially with weight loss, needs urgent assessment. See care promptly; causes include gallstones, hepatitis, and pancreatic or liver cancer.
conditions.red: pale stools, dark urine, weight loss

conditions.name: Mouth sore that won't heal
conditions.action: A mouth ulcer, red/white patch, or neck lump lasting over 3 weeks should be checked by a clinician or dentist — especially with tobacco or alcohol use. This rules out oral and head-and-neck cancers.
conditions.red: lasting over 3 weeks, neck lump, bleeding

conditions.name: Testicular lump worth checking
conditions.action: A painless lump or swelling in a testicle should be checked — testicular cancer is highly treatable when found early. See a clinician. (Sudden severe testicle pain is a separate emergency — torsion.)
conditions.red: sudden severe pain (torsion — emergency)

conditions.name: Unexplained weight loss / night sweats
conditions.action: Unexplained weight loss, drenching night sweats, and persistent fatigue should be checked. See a clinician — causes range from infection and thyroid problems to cancer; assessment finds the reason.
conditions.red: fevers, lumps, bleeding, bone pain

conditions.name: Sepsis (serious infection) — act fast
conditions.action: An infection with confusion, very fast breathing, mottled skin, or feeling extremely unwell can be sepsis — a medical emergency. Call emergency services now and say you're worried about sepsis.
conditions.red: confusion, fast breathing, mottled/blue skin, no urine

conditions.name: Fever after recent travel
conditions.action: A fever within weeks of travel abroad (especially malaria areas) needs prompt assessment — some travel infections are serious and treatable. See urgent care and mention where you travelled.
conditions.red: confusion, breathlessness, bleeding, no urine

conditions.name: Possible acute HIV / seroconversion
conditions.action: A flu-like illness with rash and swollen glands weeks after a possible exposure can be early HIV. Testing is confidential and effective treatment exists — see a clinician or sexual-health service for testing.
conditions.red: a severe headache with neck stiffness, confusion, breathlessness or a widespread rash

conditions.name: Scarlet fever
conditions.action: A fine sandpaper-like red rash with a sore throat and fever, usually in children, suggests scarlet fever — a strep infection that needs antibiotics. See a clinician.
conditions.red: very unwell, difficulty breathing

conditions.name: Carbon monoxide poisoning (consider)
conditions.action: Headache, dizziness, and nausea affecting several people (or pets) in the same building, or near fuel-burning appliances, can be carbon monoxide poisoning. Get everyone into fresh air and call emergency services now.
conditions.red: several people/pets affected, drowsiness, collapse

conditions.name: Opioid overdose
conditions.action: Pinpoint pupils with slow/absent breathing and unresponsiveness suggest an opioid overdose. Call emergency services now, give naloxone if available, and start rescue breaths/CPR if not breathing.
conditions.red: not breathing, blue lips, can't be woken

conditions.name: Poisoning / medication overdose
conditions.action: Taking too much medicine or a poison needs immediate help. Call emergency services or poison control now; have the container ready. Don't make the person vomit unless told to.
conditions.red: drowsiness, trouble breathing, seizures

conditions.name: Snake bite
conditions.action: Keep the person calm and still, keep the bitten limb below heart level, remove tight items, and get to emergency care fast — don't cut, suck, or apply a tourniquet. Note the snake's appearance if safe.
conditions.red: spreading swelling, trouble breathing, collapse

conditions.name: Animal or human bite
conditions.action: Clean a bite wound well with running water and soap. Bites easily get infected and may need antibiotics, a tetanus booster, or rabies assessment depending on the animal and region — see a clinician promptly.
conditions.red: spreading redness, fever, deep wound, wild/stray animal

conditions.name: Retinal detachment (consider)
conditions.action: A sudden shower of floaters or flashes, or a curtain/shadow moving across your vision, can be a detaching retina — a same-day eye emergency. Seek urgent eye care now to save sight.
conditions.red: a curtain over vision, sudden vision loss

conditions.name: Septic (infected) joint
conditions.action: A single hot, swollen, very painful joint with fever can be an infected joint, which can destroy the joint quickly. Seek emergency care now — don't wait to see if it settles.
conditions.red: fever with a hot swollen joint

conditions.name: Lupus (SLE) — consider
conditions.action: A butterfly rash across the cheeks with joint pain, fatigue, and sun sensitivity can suggest lupus, an autoimmune condition. See a clinician for assessment and blood tests.
conditions.red: chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache, kidney symptoms

conditions.name: Sjögren's (dry eyes & mouth)
conditions.action: Persistently dry eyes and mouth, sometimes with fatigue and joint aches, can suggest Sjögren's. See a clinician; artificial tears and saliva help symptoms.
conditions.red: severe eye pain or sudden vision change, or hot swollen salivary glands with fever

conditions.name: Raynaud's phenomenon
conditions.action: Fingers (or toes) that turn white then blue then red and go numb in the cold suggest Raynaud's. Keeping warm and avoiding triggers helps. See a clinician if ulcers form, it's one-sided, or it comes with joint/skin changes.
conditions.red: finger ulcers/sores, one-sided, with rash/joint pain

conditions.name: Myasthenia gravis (consider)
conditions.action: Muscle weakness that worsens with use and improves with rest — drooping eyelids, double vision, or trouble chewing/swallowing late in the day — can suggest myasthenia. See a clinician; sudden breathing or swallowing difficulty is an emergency.
conditions.red: trouble breathing or swallowing (emergency)

conditions.name: Guillain-Barré syndrome (consider)
conditions.action: Weakness and numbness that start in the feet and spread upward over hours-to-days, often after an infection, can be Guillain-Barré — which can affect breathing. Seek emergency care now.
conditions.red: spreading weakness, breathing or swallowing trouble

conditions.name: Menopause / perimenopause
conditions.action: Hot flushes, changing or stopping periods, sleep and mood changes in midlife suggest the menopause transition. Lifestyle measures and, for some, hormone therapy help — discuss options with a clinician. Bleeding after periods have fully stopped for a year should always be checked.
conditions.red: bleeding after menopause (needs checking)

conditions.name: Polycystic ovary syndrome (consider)
conditions.action: Irregular or absent periods with acne or excess hair and weight changes can suggest PCOS. See a clinician for assessment; managing weight, cycles, and related risks (diabetes) helps.
conditions.red: very heavy or non-stop bleeding, severe one-sided pelvic pain, or signs of pregnancy with pain

conditions.name: Endometriosis (consider)
conditions.action: Painful periods and pelvic pain that disrupt life, sometimes with pain during sex or bowel/bladder symptoms, can suggest endometriosis. See a clinician — it's under-recognized and treatable.
conditions.red: severe sudden pelvic pain, pregnancy

conditions.name: Mastitis (breast infection)
conditions.action: A red, hot, painful area of breast with fever, usually while breastfeeding, suggests mastitis. Keep feeding/expressing, rest, and fluids; antibiotics are often needed — see a clinician promptly. A fluctuant lump may be an abscess.
conditions.red: a lump/abscess, severe illness, not improving in 24h

conditions.name: Bleeding in early pregnancy
conditions.action: Bleeding and cramping in early pregnancy should be assessed promptly — it has many causes. See urgent care; one-sided pain with faintness can be an ectopic pregnancy (an emergency).
conditions.red: one-sided pain, faintness, shoulder-tip pain, heavy bleeding

conditions.name: Adrenal (Addisonian) crisis
conditions.action: In someone with adrenal insufficiency, vomiting, severe weakness, dizziness, or confusion can be an adrenal crisis. Give emergency steroid (hydrocortisone) if prescribed for emergencies and call emergency services now.
conditions.red: collapse, confusion, persistent vomiting

conditions.name: Cushing's syndrome (consider)
conditions.action: Weight gain around the trunk and face, purple stretch marks, easy bruising, and high blood pressure can suggest excess cortisol (Cushing's). See a clinician for assessment.
conditions.red: severe headache with vision change, black stools, or severe weakness and confusion

conditions.name: Easy bruising / bleeding — assess
conditions.action: Unexplained easy bruising, bleeding gums, frequent nosebleeds, or tiny red skin spots should be checked with blood tests — causes range from medication to platelet or clotting problems and, rarely, blood cancers.
conditions.red: heavy or uncontrolled bleeding, widespread spots + fever

conditions.name: Heavy menstrual bleeding
conditions.action: Very heavy periods can cause tiredness and low iron. Several treatments help — see a clinician. Flooding with dizziness or breathlessness needs prompt review.
conditions.red: dizziness, breathlessness, soaking pads hourly

conditions.name: Occasional palpitations (usually benign)
conditions.action: Occasional skipped or extra beats when you're otherwise well are usually harmless, often with caffeine, stress, or tiredness. See a clinician if they're frequent, come with chest pain, breathlessness, or fainting, or you have heart disease.
conditions.red: fainting, chest pain, breathlessness with them

conditions.name: Simple faint (vasovagal)
conditions.action: Fainting with warning (feeling hot, nauseated, tunnel vision) after standing, pain, or emotion is usually a simple faint. Lie down and raise the legs at the warning. Fainting with NO warning, during exertion, or with chest pain/palpitations needs urgent cardiac assessment.
conditions.red: faint during exercise, no warning, or with chest pain/palpitations

conditions.name: Nosebleed
conditions.action: For a nosebleed, sit forward and pinch the soft part of the nose firmly for 10-15 minutes without letting go, breathing through the mouth. Seek care if it won't stop after 20-30 minutes, is very heavy, follows a head injury, or you're on blood thinners.
conditions.red: won't stop after 20-30 min, heavy, on blood thinners, after head injury

conditions.name: Contact dermatitis
conditions.action: An itchy rash exactly where something touched the skin (jewellery, cosmetics, plants) suggests contact dermatitis. Avoid the trigger, wash the area, and moisturizers or short steroid-cream courses help. Spreading infection or facial/eye involvement needs care.
conditions.red: spreading redness/pus, face or eyes involved

conditions.name: Acne
conditions.action: Spots on the face, chest, or back are common, especially in teens. Gentle washing and OTC products (benzoyl peroxide, salicylic acid) help — see the medication reference and follow the label. Severe, scarring, or distressing acne is very treatable — see a clinician.
conditions.red: scarring, severe, or causing distress

conditions.name: Cold sore (oral herpes)
conditions.action: A tingling then blistering sore on the lip is usually a cold sore (herpes simplex). Antiviral creams work best started at the tingle stage. Avoid touching/sharing; it's contagious. Sores near the eye, or widespread/severe, need a clinician.
conditions.red: near the eye, widespread, immune-compromised

conditions.name: Coeliac disease (consider)
conditions.action: Bloating, loose stools, tiredness, or weight changes linked to wheat/gluten can suggest coeliac disease. Keep eating gluten and ask a clinician to test before changing diet (stopping gluten first can hide it).
conditions.red: weight loss, anaemia, blood in stool

conditions.name: Persistent bloating / pelvic symptoms
conditions.action: Persistent bloating, feeling full quickly, or pelvic pressure most days for weeks should be checked — most causes are benign, but this rules out ovarian cancer. See a clinician.
conditions.red: persistent bloating/pressure for 3+ weeks

conditions.name: Persistent indigestion + weight loss
conditions.action: Persistent indigestion with unintended weight loss, feeling full quickly, or vomiting should be checked to rule out stomach or oesophageal cancer. See a clinician.
conditions.red: weight loss, vomiting, black stools, trouble swallowing

conditions.name: New persistent/progressive headache + neuro signs
conditions.action: New headaches that are persistent or progressive — especially worse in the morning, with vomiting, vision/speech change, weakness, personality change, or a first seizure — should be assessed. See a clinician; a first seizure or sudden severe headache is urgent.
conditions.red: first seizure, morning vomiting, weakness, sudden severe headache

conditions.name: Iron-deficiency anaemia
conditions.action: Tiredness, paleness, breathlessness on exertion, and sometimes craving ice can point to low iron. Iron-rich foods help and a blood test confirms it — see a clinician, who will also look for the cause (e.g. heavy periods, gut bleeding). See the nutrition guide for iron-rich foods.
conditions.red: black stools, heavy periods, breathless at rest

conditions.name: Vitamin B12 / folate deficiency
conditions.action: Fatigue with a sore smooth tongue, tingling in the hands/feet, or memory changes can suggest B12 or folate deficiency (common with vegan diets, older age, or absorption problems). A blood test confirms it; treatment is effective — see a clinician. Nerve symptoms shouldn't be left untreated.
conditions.red: worsening numbness/balance, confusion

conditions.name: Vitamin D deficiency
conditions.action: Aching bones and muscles with tiredness, especially with little sun exposure, can suggest low vitamin D. Supplements and some sun help; a blood test confirms it. See the nutrition guide — many people, including all babies, are advised a daily vitamin D supplement.
conditions.red: severe bone pain, fractures, muscle weakness

conditions.name: Undernutrition / malnutrition
conditions.action: Eating too little over time, with weight loss and weakness, is undernutrition — it slows healing and weakens the body. Small, frequent, nourishing meals help; see a clinician to find why (illness, dental, mood, swallowing, money) and get support. See the nutrition guide for your age.
conditions.red: rapid weight loss, falls, unable to eat/drink

conditions.name: Infant not gaining weight (failure to thrive)
conditions.action: A baby who isn't gaining weight or growing as expected needs assessment — causes include feeding difficulty, intake, or an underlying condition. See a clinician or health visitor promptly; keep offering feeds. See the infant nutrition guide.
conditions.red: poor feeding, few wet nappies, floppy or drowsy

conditions.name: Vitamin C deficiency (scurvy)
conditions.action: Very low vitamin C over months — rare, but seen with very limited diets — causes bruising, bleeding gums, aching, and poor healing. It reverses quickly with vitamin C (fruit/veg or a supplement). See a clinician. See the nutrition guide.
conditions.red: bleeding gums with a very limited diet

conditions.name: Weight & healthy eating (support)
conditions.action: If you want to eat more healthily or are concerned about your weight, that's worth support — and it's about overall health and how you feel, not a number. Small sustainable changes, balanced meals, movement you enjoy, and a clinician or dietitian's help work better than crash diets. See the nutrition guide for your age.
conditions.red: fainting, chest pain, or signs of an eating disorder such as purging or collapse

conditions.name: Cut / laceration (bleeding wound)
conditions.action: Press firmly and continuously on the wound with a clean cloth for a full 10–15 minutes without lifting to peek, and raise the area above heart level if you can. Once bleeding slows, rinse a minor cut under clean running water and pat dry. Get it checked for stitches if it is deep or gaping, keeps bleeding, is longer than about 1 cm on the face or 2 cm elsewhere, was caused by something dirty or a bite, or if your tetanus shots aren't up to date. To dress it: cover with a clean non-stick pad, hold it on with tape or a bandage that is snug but not tight enough to cut off circulation (the fingers or toes past it should stay warm and pink), and change the dressing if it soaks through or at least daily. Watch for infection — spreading redness, warmth, pus, or fever.
conditions.red: Bleeding that won't stop after 15 minutes of firm pressure, blood that spurts or soaks through, a deep or gaping wound, numbness or not being able to move past the cut, or feeling faint — get emergency help.

conditions.name: Genital injury
conditions.action: Injuries to the penis, scrotum or genital area can bleed heavily and can affect the tube you urinate through, so this should be looked at in person. Apply gentle but firm pressure with a clean cloth to control bleeding and support the area. Be seen promptly — go to urgent care or the ER for anything more than a minor graze, for heavy bleeding, trouble passing urine, blood at the opening, or severe pain or swelling. To dress it: cover with a clean non-stick pad, hold it on with tape or a bandage that is snug but not tight enough to cut off circulation (the fingers or toes past it should stay warm and pink), and change the dressing if it soaks through or at least daily. Watch for infection — spreading redness, warmth, pus, or fever.
conditions.red: Heavy bleeding that won't stop, being unable to pass urine, blood at the tip, or sudden severe pain or swelling of a testicle — treat as an emergency.

conditions.name: Serious burn — act fast
conditions.action: This looks like a serious (deep or large) burn — call your local emergency number now. Keep cooling the burn with cool running water, cover it loosely with cling film or a clean non-fluffy sheet, keep the rest of the person warm and still, and do not apply creams or break blisters.
conditions.red: Trouble breathing, soot or burns around the mouth or nose, a hoarse voice, burns over a large area, or the person becoming drowsy or pale — emergency.

conditions.name: Tooth / dental problem
conditions.action: Toothache usually means a cavity, a cracked tooth, or an infection, and needs a dentist. For relief meanwhile: simple pain relief, avoid very hot, cold or sweet foods, and keep the area clean. See a dentist soon.
conditions.red: Spreading face or gum swelling, fever, or trouble swallowing or breathing — a dental infection can spread, so get urgent medical care.

conditions.name: Urinary incontinence (leaking)
conditions.action: Leaking urine is common and very treatable — you don't have to live with it. Pelvic-floor (Kegel) exercises help most types; cutting caffeine and treating constipation help too. A clinician can work out the type (leaking with coughing vs a sudden urge) and the best options.
conditions.red: New leaking together with back pain, numbness between the legs, or being unable to pass urine at all — see someone urgently (possible nerve problem).

conditions.name: Neck strain / mechanical neck pain
conditions.action: Most neck pain is muscular and eases over days to a couple of weeks. Keep moving it gently rather than holding it stiff, use heat, check your pillow and screen height, and simple pain relief helps.
conditions.red: Neck pain after a real injury, with arm weakness or numbness, loss of bladder or bowel control, a fever with a stiff neck, or a sudden 'worst-ever' headache — get seen urgently.

conditions.name: Breast pain
conditions.action: Breast pain is very common and is usually not cancer — it's often hormonal (worse before a period) or muscular. A well-fitting supportive bra, simple pain relief, and noting it against your cycle help. See a clinician if it's one-sided and constant, or comes with a lump or skin/nipple change.
conditions.red: A new lump, skin dimpling, nipple change or discharge, or one spot that is always painful — get it checked.

conditions.name: Nail or hair problem
conditions.action: Nail and hair problems have many causes — fungal infection, iron or thyroid issues, stress, or simply age — and are rarely urgent. A clinician can look for a treatable cause (for example iron or thyroid tests for hair loss, or antifungal treatment for nails).
conditions.red: Sudden patchy hair loss with scarring of the scalp, or a nail that has newly turned dark or streaked — get it checked.

conditions.name: Insect sting / bite
